newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-HULL RETURNS FROM BENCHING TO SCORE GAME WINNER FOR BLUES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-HULL RETURNS FROM BENCHING TO SCORE GAME WINNER FOR BLUES.

text.p: St Louis star Brett Hull, who is reportedly on the trading block, returned from a highly publicised benching to score the winning goal for the Blues on Sunday.

Hull, who was scratched from the Blues' lineup Friday despite being healthy, scored his 12th goal of the season midway through the final period to lift St Louis to a 3-2 victory over the Edmonton Oilers.
Hull took a pass from Peter Zezel, raced in ahead of an Edmonton defender and fired the puck from the low slot over goaltender Curtis Joseph to snap a 2-2 tie.
The Blues sniper, who reportedly has given the club a list of teams to which he would accept a trade, is three tallies shy of the career 500-goal plateau.
Zezel and Joe Murphy scored first-period goals to stake St Louis to a 2-0 lead.

Andrei Kovalenko cut the lead in half with a powerplay goal 2:49 into the second. Jason Arnott got the tying goal with 3:10 left in the middle frame when he beat Edmonton goalie Grant Fuhr on a breakaway.
Fuhr made 28 saves for the Blues. Joseph finished with 24 saves.
St Louis coach and General Manager Mike Keenan, who is often at odds with his star player, and Hull both tried to defuse the latest controversy after the game.
"He's a great player, very dangerous. If he gets an inch, he has the ability to win hockey games for us and that's what he did tonight," Keenan of Hull.
Hull said he and Keenan had a meeting Sunday to clear the air. "(He) told me to just relax, to not let things get to me," Hull said.
"I've never said anything bad about Mike because he and I want the same things -- we both just want to win."
At Florida, Greg Adams scored 59 seconds into the third period to lift the Dallas Stars into a 1-1 tie with the Panthers in a tight-checking game that featured few scoring opportunities.

Adams and Mike Modano broke into the Panthers' zone on a 2-on-1. Modano carried the puck down the right wing before sliding it into the slot, where Adams poked it through John Vanbiesbrouck's pads for his 12th goal of the season.

Mike Hough scored the lone Florida goal with 3:04 left in the first period. He fired a blast from just outside the Dallas blue line, but Stars goalie Andy Moog, playing with a slight groin pull, had difficulty moving to his left and the puck beat him low to the glove side.
Vanbiesbrouck made 21 saves, including four in overtime. Moog faced just 19 shots as the Panthers were held to only two shots on goal in the third period.
The Stars lost defenceman Derian Hatcher, who suffered a sprained left knee in the second period and did not return.
